public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 972

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/972](https://www.erdosproblems.com/972)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos972

/--
The set of primes `p` such that `Nat.floor (α * p)` is also prime.
-/
def primeSet (α : ℝ) : Set ℕ :=
  {p : ℕ | Nat.Prime p ∧ Nat.Prime ⌊ (α * p) ⌋₊}

/--
**Erdős problem 972.**
Let $\alpha > 1$ be irrational. Are there infinitely many primes $p$
such that $\lfloor p\alpha \rfloor$ is also prime?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_972 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ α > 1, Irrational α → (primeSet α).Infinite := by
  sorry

end Erdos972

reformulations.difference: Lean uses natural-number floor and Nat.Prime rather than ordinary integer floor.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For α > 1 and p : ℕ, α * p is nonnegative, so (Nat.floor (α * p) : ℤ) equals the ordinary integer floor of p * α. Primality of this natural number agrees with primality of its integer cast. Thus the prime sets, and consequently the universally quantified infinitude statements, agree exactly.
